theme: दिव्य मित्रता से शांति | Peace through seeing the Divine as friend
context: At the close of Chapter 5, after describing steadiness amid changing experiences and freedom from the pull of desire and anger, Krishna gives Arjuna a concise way to understand peace: know Krishna as the recipient of sacrifice and austerity, the great Lord of all worlds, and the friend of every being. This verse closes the chapter; the next chapter begins with a discussion of action and renunciation.
contextHindi: पाँचवें अध्याय के अंत में, सुख-दुःख और इच्छा-क्रोध से ऊपर उठने की चर्चा के बाद, कृष्ण शांति की एक संक्षिप्त समझ देते हैं। वे अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि उन्हें यज्ञ और तप का भोक्ता, सब लोकों का महान अधिपति और सभी प्राणियों का हितैषी जानने वाला शांति पाता है। यहीं अध्याय समाप्त होता है; अगला अध्याय कर्म और संन्यास की चर्चा से शुरू होगा।
sanskritDevanagari:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् |
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ||५-२९||
transliteration:
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram .
suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati ||5-29||

wordByWord.meaning: The one who receives or partakes of; here, the recipient of yajña and tapas.
Sacrifice or offering; its precise form depends on context and practice.
The great Lord of all worlds, as Krishna describes himself in this verse.
A well-wisher or friend; one who desires the good of others.
Peace or inner calm; the verse presents it as the result of knowing Krishna in these ways.

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में कृष्ण अपनी पहचान तीन तरह से बताते हैं: यज्ञ और तप के भोक्ता, सब लोकों के महान अधिपति, और सभी प्राणियों के सुहृद—यानी उनके हित की कामना करने वाले मित्र। फिर वे कहते हैं कि जो उन्हें इस रूप में जानता है, वह शांति पाता है। यहाँ “जानना” केवल कोई बात सुन लेना नहीं, बल्कि जीवन और कर्म को उस समझ के अनुसार देखना भी हो सकता है। यज्ञ का अर्थ अर्पण या समर्पित कर्म है, और तप का अर्थ अनुशासित साधना; इनका एक ही बाहरी रूप सबके लिए तय नहीं किया गया है। पाठ की बात साफ है: कृष्ण अपने बारे में यह दावा करते हैं और इस ज्ञान को शांति से जोड़ते हैं। इसे हर कठिनाई मिटने की वैज्ञानिक गारंटी समझना उचित नहीं होगा। एक सावधान निष्कर्ष यह है कि कर्म को केवल निजी लाभ के लिए न देखकर, व्यापक हित और किसी विश्वसनीय नैतिक दिशा से जोड़ना मन को अधिक स्थिर कर सकता है। “सभी प्राणियों का मित्र” कहना हमें दूसरों के प्रति सद्भाव की याद दिलाता है, न कि किसी को अपनी मान्यता मानने के लिए बाध्य करता है।
clearEnglish: Krishna closes the chapter by naming three relationships to the Divine: offerings and disciplined practices are directed toward Him; He is sovereign over all worlds; and He is the well-wisher of every being. The verse says that knowing Him in these ways leads to peace. “Knowing” can suggest more than repeating a description: it can shape how a person understands responsibility, power, and the lives of others. Still, we should keep the claim in its proper frame. TEXT: Krishna speaks of himself in these terms and connects this recognition with peace. The verse does not offer an empirical guarantee that devotion will remove every hardship, nor does it specify one required form of sacrifice or austerity. INFERENCE: If actions are understood as offerings rather than possessions, and ultimate power is associated with goodwill toward all beings, a practitioner may find less reason to act from self-importance or hostility. This is a spiritual interpretation, not a substitute for evidence or practical help when someone is suffering. The verse’s closing emphasis on friendship also invites an ethical question: does one’s religious understanding deepen care for others, including those beyond one’s own community?

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Krishna identifies himself as the recipient of yajña and tapas, the great Lord of all worlds, and the well-wisher of all beings; the verse says that knowing him this way brings peace.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Seeing disciplined action as an offering and grounding authority in goodwill may encourage humility and care. This is a reasonable application, not a separate promise stated in the verse or an empirical guarantee.

practicalApplication.label: Offer one action
practicalApplication.text: Choose one ordinary task today and do it carefully as a contribution, not merely as a way to gain praise or control the outcome.

practicalApplication.label: Practice goodwill
practicalApplication.text: Before responding to someone difficult, pause and ask what a response guided by their genuine well-being, as well as your own boundaries, would look like.

reflectionQuestion: If you took seriously the idea that the Divine is a well-wisher of every being, what might change in one way you treat someone today?
reflectionQuestionHindi: अगर आप सचमुच मानें कि दिव्य सत्ता सभी प्राणियों की हितैषी है, तो आज किसी एक व्यक्ति के साथ आपके व्यवहार में क्या बदलाव आ सकता है?
